paper_metadata.title: Predicting intracerebral hemorrhage by baseline magnetic resonance imaging in stroke patients undergoing systemic thrombolysis

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes the setting well. However, it is a retrospective database review with a significant exclusion rate (20.5%) due to image quality, which may introduce selection bias if those with poor images differed clinically from those included.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: We screened our internal database containing patients admitted to the stroke unit of the University of Leipzig between January 2005 and December 2008 for eligible candidates.
items.reasoning: The source is a specific university hospital stroke unit database with a defined timeframe.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: We screened our internal database containing patients admitted to the stroke unit... Inclusion criteria were the following: (i) Sudden onset of a focal neurological deficit... (ii) Systemic treatment with tPA... (iii) cerebral MRI containing at least DWI, FLAIR and T2*... (iv) cerebral CT performed within 24 h
items.reasoning: The recruitment process from an internal database using specific clinical and imaging criteria is well-defined.

items.reasoning: Criteria include clinical symptoms, treatment type, timing (zero time), and specific imaging requirements.

items.reasoning: 25 out of 122 eligible patients (20.5%) were excluded due to technical issues. While common in MRI studies, this is a significant portion of the eligible sample.

(NIHSS) and time from symptom onset to tPA administration.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (FLAIR and DWI) were measured using standardized MRI protocols and assessed by blinded independent raters with high inter-rater agreement.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: presence and size of FLAIRpositive lesions located within the area of restricted DWI also demonstrating lowered ADC values.
items.reasoning: The prognostic factor is clearly defined based on specific MRI sequence characteristics.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Two neurologists examined – independently from each other and in a blinded manner... The overall inter-rater agreement for evaluation of cerebral imaging was similarly high for FLAIR status (0.76)
items.reasoning: Blinded independent assessment and high Kappa scores support reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: stratified to the following groups depending on the proportion of DWI-restricted area with reference to the whole supplying territory of the affected cerebral artery: <1/3 (n = 62), 1/3–2/3 (n = 18) and >2/3 (n = 17).
items.reasoning: The 1/3 territory cut-off is a standard clinical metric in stroke (derived from ECASS/ASPECTS logic).

items.reasoning: A standardized protocol and single scanner type were used for all.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (ICH) was defined using established international criteria (ECASS II) and assessed by blinded raters using objective CT imaging.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: classified first in the existence or non-existence of any ICH and second according to the ECASS II criteria: Hemorrhagic infarction 1... parenchymal hemorrhage... Clinical deterioration of at least four points at the NIHSS... was considered indicative of symptomatic ICH.
items.reasoning: The study uses both radiologic (ECASS II) and clinical (NIHSS change) definitions for the outcome.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome

items.evidence_snippet: Two neurologists examined... in a blinded manner... An independent neuroradiologist – also blinded to further patients' characteristics – reevaluated MRI or CT scans in cases of inconsistent ratings
items.reasoning: Blinding and expert adjudication were used to ensure reliability.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The follow-up CT scan... was performed as a 5 mm slice axial scan... on a 64-slice CT scanner
items.reasoning: A standardized CT protocol was used for all participants.
